physical.title: skirt (skirt cloth); kain
physical.summary: A cotton (tabby) batik skirt cloth, a 'kain panjang'; hand-drawn on both sides, unsewn.  Decorated with a bold all-over pattern of large flower shapes on stems in bands across the width of the cloth, with stems alternately at top and bottom of cloth.  Stems and outlines in indigo black, petals in soga, seed heads and detail in some petals in white.  Isen pattern filling entire background is gringsing with cross in each scale.  Plain white band around whole edge.  [Text written by Dr Fiona Kerlogue, Horniman Museum.]

physical.title: skirt (skirt cloth); kain
physical.summary: A (tabby) cotton skirt cloth, a kain panjang, decorated in hand-drawn batik.  Hemmed at both short ends.  Background filling motif is gringsing against which are set vertical columns of larger motifs, alternating between columns made up of sections of a circle, almost a stylised lar, with concentric bands of patterning, and columns of more fragmentary motifs drawn from classical semen designs arranged neatly one above the other.  Finely glazed.  An accomplished piece of work.  [Text written by Dr Fiona Kerlogue, Horniman Museum.]

cultural.vision_reason: This is a hand-drawn batik cotton sarong with a north-coast Javanese style kepala/badan design, described as such in the museum record; batik sarongs like this are worn across Java and Bali and are plausible Balinese dress, matching the claimed garment category.

physical.title: skirt; sarong
physical.summary: A cotton (tabby) batik tube skirt, a 'sarung', hand-drawn, mostly one-sided?  Probably from north coast, in strong colours, crudely finished.  'Kepala' has blue background, scalloped sides separated from blue inner border only by a very narrow scalloped strip achieved, as with most of the design in the 'kepala' and within border, in very dark red, probably produced by overpainting the blue.  Design in 'kepala' originally outlined in narrow line of wax, some parts which remain white filled in with wax, mainly some of the large petals of the main flower design in the 'kepala', some scattered small flowers and part of the wings of a butterfly.  The 'kepala' is only 8 cms away from the right hand edge of the cloth. Top border, which has a straight edge, is in dark brown with blue and white detailing.  'Badan' is of diagonal bands, the widest with a striped background, just off vertical, against which are set highly stylised shapes which may be animal or floral.  Another set of bands are gringsing (scales) with leaf shapes set against them. Between these two types are narrower bands in threes, blue triangles on the outer and dark stripes on the inner.  Narrow sisir stripes along long edges.   [Text written by Dr Fiona Kerlogue, Horniman Museum.]

cultural.vision_reason: Hand-drawn batik sarong with kepala (triangular pointed panel), papan, and badan sections in classic brown/blue/cream Javanese-style batik coloring — a form of sarong cloth also worn traditionally in Bali, consistent with the claimed Balinese garment attribution.

physical.title: skirt (unsewn); sarong (unsewn)
physical.summary: A (tabby) cotton skirt cloth, a sarung, previously stitched into a tube but now unstitched.  Decorated in hand-drawn batik, with central kepala, space between triangles filled with background filling design, isen, of k.o. ukel pattern, and design of pointed motif in cream, soga and blue detailing.  Papan have flowers and three-leaved motifs alternating in cream, blue and soga on dark blue ground.  Border to top and bottom of cloth and continuing along vertical borders of papan of scrolling stylised flowers with thorny stem.  Badan has large structural design more or less symmetrical about a horizontal axis, suggestive of two supporting columns with two branches above, these in dark blue, decorated with soga patterning and white detailing.  Surrounding this structure is an isen of gringsing against which are semen patterns and lar, the latter uni-directional suggesting which way up the cloth would have been worn.  Has narrow fold at each short side.   [Text written by Dr Fiona Kerlogue, Horniman Museum.]

physical.title: skirt (unsewn); sarong (unsewn)
physical.summary: A batik tube skirt, a sarung, made from tabby cotton cloth; unsewn, hand-drawn.  Central kepala has triangles with alternating cream and light blue ground enclosing floral and foliate shapes in black and blue.  Black area between triangles with star and paku shapes. Sembagi-like pattern above and below in borders, which continue up outer side of papan.  Papan enclosed in frame of curlicue motifs in cream on black ground; papan themselves have phoenixes in same colour scheme.  Badan includes sawat shapes at an angle, also groups of squares with serrated edges in threes, fours, fives, sixes, sevens in various arrangements.  Background filled with gringsing.  All in blue/black on cream ground.  Red veining shows red dyed last.  [Text written by Dr Fiona Kerlogue, Horniman Museum.]
